title: RapidChart clinical feedback, April 13
subtitle: Allergies before meds, ED discharge lag, and what nurses do not care about
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Engineering, Rahul Deshmukh (PM), Denise Howell (nursing informatics), QA
owners: Aman Kumar (notes), Rahul Deshmukh (priority calls), Kavya Menon (assemble order)
summary: Working notes from the April 13 feedback session at RVH-MAIN with Denise Howell, two charge nurses, Dr. Anita Shah, Rahul Deshmukh, and Aman Kumar. Nurses do not care that we built a unified patient API. They care that allergies render before medications, and that the ED tracker still shows discharged patients for about 11 min. We left with two P0s (allergy block order, ED discharge lag), one P2 (pretty demographics), and an open question on a 'record incomplete' banner. These notes are the source of truth for tickets RVH-2184 and RVH-2201 until the PRD is patched.

blocks.text: Rahul opened with a slide titled Unified patient API, six months in. Marisol asked, before he finished the second bullet, whether this meeting was about the thing that still puts meds on the screen before allergies. It was. We put the slide away at 15:14. The rest of the hour was RapidChart as nurses use it on a Tuesday afternoon, not the service catalog. That is the useful part. The API work is real (RVH-PRD-2020-019) and none of the people drawing meds cared about the unification story. Anita said that out loud so we would write it down.
You can call it one API in your ticket. On the floor I need the allergy block up before I touch the pyxis. If meds paint first I have already started the wrong habit.

blocks.text: Priya Nair was not in the room. Rahul briefed her April 14. She agreed the two P0s are engineering work, not 'nursing preference.' Error budget and the 1.8s assemble SLO stay. Allergy-first is an ordering change inside an already-fetched payload for RapidChart's main view. It should not spend SLO. Discharge lag might, if we start hammering ChartLine. That is called out under risks.
What we watched on the workstation

Denise logged into RapidChart staging against patient-api 1.11.4 with SYNTH-000441. Network throttling was off. Time to first paint of the meds block was 1.16s. Time to first paint of the allergy block was 1.94s, because the UI awaits the meds column template before it mounts allergies. That is a frontend sequence, not a ChartLine sequence. Kavya confirmed assemble already returns allergies in the JSON before meds (payload.blocks order: demo, allergy, med, enc, prob). RapidChart 4.3.1 ignores that order and mounts meds first because the 2020 prototype used a two-column layout with meds on the left. Nobody told the floor we had 'fixed' allergies in the API in January. They cannot see JSON.

Patrice had a live complaint from RVH-WEST med-surg, not synth. A patient with a documented penicillin allergy had the meds list on screen for 'a couple of seconds' (we did not measure WEST today) while allergies still showed the spinner. She does not want a spinner on allergies if meds are already interactive. Anita agreed: interactive meds plus spinning allergies is worse than both spinning, because it invites the pyxis walk. Sneha was not present; Aman will ask her to add a UI timing assertion, not only an API body assertion, in RVH-QA-2021-007.
ED tracker, discharged names

Marisol walked us to an ED workstation (MAIN-ED-14) on CensusBoard 2.8.6. She discharged a test encounter at 15:51:20. The name stayed on the 'in department' board until 16:02:38. That is 11 min 18s. She said that is typical, 'about eleven minutes,' sometimes 9, sometimes 14 if ChartLine is 'having a day.' She uses those minutes to call bed control and gets asked why a discharged patient is still occupying a bay on the board. Charge nurses have been paper-taping over names. That is the incident, not the API branding.

We already knew from RVH-INC-2021-118 adjacent work that census inflation and discharge lag share a ChartLine ADT path, but they are not the same ticket. Inflation was a count bug. This is a freshness bug on a named row. Chris Patel's February measurement on ADT topic chartline.adt.discharge was 6.2 min p50, 11.4 min p95 to the moment patient-api wrote census:discharged:* in Redis. Redis TTL on those keys is 90s. So most of the 11 min is upstream of us. We can still stop adding our own 90s, and we can still poll ChartLine's discharge status on a shorter loop for ED facilities only. That is the engineering argument. Marisol does not care which hop we cut. She cares that the name is gone before the next ambulance.

blocks.text: The 'unified API' moment

Rahul's opening slide had three bullets about one payload, one auth story, and one SLA. Marisol's response was that she has three systems on the ED desk and she will keep having three systems, and the only SLA she feels is whether allergies show. Anita backed her: the CMIO office asked Northstar for a safer assemble path, not a branding campaign. Aman said we should keep the unified API work internally (versioning, LDAP, feed isolation) and change the nursing-facing narrative to 'chart blocks in a safe order, with honest banners.' Rahul agreed, slightly late. This is recorded so the next QBR deck does not reopen it.

Rejected alternative: keep the current RapidChart mount order and add a yellow 'check allergies' toast once meds render. Kavya sketched it in 4 minutes on Zoom. Denise said toasts are ignored, and Marisol said ED already has too many toasts from bed control. The toast dies. We will change mount order. If RapidChart 4.3.1 cannot mount allergy first without a layout rewrite, that rewrite is still P0, not a reason to toast.

Allergy-first: engineering translation

payload.blocks from patient-api 1.11.4 is already demo, allergy, med, enc, prob. RapidChart ChartView.jsx (their repo, we have read-only) maps blocks to columns with an explicit list ['med','allergy','enc','prob','demo'] for the 'clinical first' layout they shipped in November 2020. They believed meds were the 'clinical first' field. Nursing at this meeting said otherwise for the opening view. Problems list can stay below. Encounters (last 5) can stay below. Demographics header can stay in the chrome; they did not complain about header timing, only about pretty formatting, which is P2.

Two implementation paths. Path A: Riverview RapidChart team reorders the mount list. We would file in their Jira (project RCHART) and wait. Their last three UI tickets took 19, 24, and 41 days. Path B: we send a response header X-RVH-Block-Priority: allergy,med and they already have a stub to honor it (comment in ChartView.jsx dated 2021-01-07, never wired). Kavya can ship the header in 1.12.0. Aman will talk to their app lead (Gita Raman, Riverview, not Northstar) April 16. If Gita will wire the stub by April 28, we do both: header plus their one-line reorder. If she cannot, we still ship the header and Denise will escalate on the Riverview side. We do not fork RapidChart.

SiteNotes being flaky on Fridays does not change allergy-first. Allergies do not come from SiteNotes. If ChartLine allergy is down, the allergy block must fail loud, not wait on meds, not wait on notes. Partial fill rules in RVH-PRD-2021-006 already say that. Today's meeting adds: the UI must not make meds look 'ready' while that loud fail is still spinning.

Record incomplete banner (open)

Denise wants a persistent banner when any of allergies, meds, or problems is missing because a source is down. Copy she proposed on the whiteboard: 'Record incomplete. Do not assume missing allergies.' Anita said the second sentence is the kind of thing malpractice counsel will rewrite, and also that 'do not assume missing allergies' is clinically right. She will send the sentence to Riverview legal (contact she named: Owen Brant, not present) and to Helen Park if the banner implies we know the record is wrong rather than incomplete. Difference matters for disclosure.

Engineering can show a banner from payload.banners[] which already exists in the assemble contract (RVH-PRD-2021-006). We should not invent a second banner channel. The open question is only whether RapidChart is required to show banners[type=record_incomplete] on every partial, and what the string is. Until May 4 we keep current banners (source-specific: chartline_unavailable, sitenotes_unavailable, feed_disabled). We do not ship record_incomplete in 1.12.0.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Do not treat 'no known allergies' as the fallback when ChartLine allergy fails. That string is a clinical assertion. Partial fill must not collapse into it. If you find a code path that does, it is a Sev-1, not a copy tweak. Anita was explicit.

Conversation notes that are not decisions
These are here so we do not lose tone. They are not commitments.

Anita: ChartLine still cannot emit FHIR. Vendors in the room last October pushed R4. The floor does not ask for FHIR. She does not want us to reopen RVH-TDD-2020-011 because a payer webinar said 'FHIR year.' If a payer or HIE mandates it, that is a different project with a different budget. Noted.

Denise: Friday afternoons SiteNotes is 'always junk.' She already knows RapidChart banners notes and not the whole chart. She wants the same honesty for allergies. She will train charge nurses on banner text if we freeze the strings for 90 days at a time. We should not A/B banner copy on a live unit.

Marisol: the 11 min lag is worst at 15:00-19:00 when discharges cluster. Overnight is quieter. Any load test Sneha runs at 10:00 will understate ED pain. Sneha should pick a 16:30 window on staging with a discharge burst. Aman will put that in the QA ticket.

Patrice: WEST med-surg still sees hyphenated surnames split across two header lines, which she called 'ugly' and then 'fine if allergies work.' That is the P2. Do not let RVH-2190 jump the queue because it is visible in screenshots for executives.

Kavya (Zoom): assemble p95 on prod last week was 1.62s. Reordering JSON keys does nothing for RapidChart. Header X-RVH-Block-Priority is cheap. She does not want to hold 1.12.0 for CensusBoard work. Split the trains. Agreed in the room.

Rahul: he will rewrite the steering slide before Thursday's Riverview IT ops forum. Aman will sanity-check the slide for leftover 'unified' as the lead. Chris Patel will send Denise a one-page on how we measure ADT lag, without MRNs.
